_meta.description: Point-in-time state AI governance and transparency record. Populated entries must cite official state sources; Unknown rows are launch scaffolding for future official-source review.
_meta.scopeNote: Planning and reference aid only. Entries summarize official state public records located for this project; they do not determine legal applicability, compliance status, or whether an agency has fully disclosed every AI use.

federalContext.title: Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
federalContext.summary: The federal-versus-state AI governance picture is in flux. EO 14365 was signed on December 11, 2025 and published on December 16, 2025, and directs a national AI policy framework review that may affect state AI laws and disclosure requirements.

mandates.title: Executive Order N-5-26: Trusted AI Procurement
mandates.citation: Executive Department, State of California, Executive Order N-5-26
mandates.summary: California directs state procurement and technology agencies to recommend AI vendor certifications, share responsible AI procurement and adoption practices, expand vetted GenAI access and training for state workers, update the State Digital Strategy, pilot AI-supported government-service access, publish a data minimization toolkit, and issue watermarking guidance.

mandates.title: Public Act No. 23-16: Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy
mandates.summary: Connecticut requires executive-branch and judicial-branch inventories of AI systems, public posting of those inventories, policies and procedures for AI development, procurement, implementation, use and ongoing assessment, and impact assessments before covered AI systems are implemented.

mandates.title: State of Indiana Artificial Intelligence Policy and Guidance
mandates.citation: Office of the Indiana Chief Data Officer, State of Indiana AI Policy and Guidance
mandates.summary: Indiana has adopted an enterprise policy for AI use within state government. State employees may use only AI systems assessed and approved by the Office of the Chief Data Officer; agencies submit AI Readiness Assessment materials before implementation or use, and approved exceptions are reevaluated annually.

mandates.title: Catalyzing the Responsible and Productive Use of Artificial Intelligence in Maryland State Government
mandates.citation: Governor of Maryland, Artificial Intelligence Executive Order
mandates.summary: Maryland establishes principles for AI use in state agencies, including fairness and equity, innovation, privacy, safety, transparency, accountability, and human-centered government service. The order establishes an AI Subcabinet to develop and implement a comprehensive AI action plan and guardrails for agency use.

mandates.title: Executive Order No. 629: Establishing an Artificial Intelligence Strategic Task Force
mandates.citation: Commonwealth of Massachusetts Executive Order No. 629
mandates.summary: Massachusetts established an AI Strategic Task Force to study AI and generative AI impacts on the state, including effects on state employees, constituents, private business, and higher education, collect stakeholder input, and advise the Governor and executive branch through a written report.

mandates.title: Public Artificial Intelligence Services Security Standard
mandates.citation: Minnesota IT Services, Public Artificial Intelligence Services Security Standard
mandates.summary: Minnesota's AI security standard guides responsible use of public AI services by state employees and applies to employees, contractors, and third parties who develop, deploy, or use AI systems and applications within state government. It focuses on secure use, productivity, and protection of private, sensitive, or protected data.

mandates.title: Executive Order No. 346: Artificial Intelligence Task Force
mandates.citation: State of New Jersey Executive Order No. 346
mandates.summary: New Jersey established an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to study emerging AI technologies, issue findings on societal impacts, recommend government actions for ethical and responsible AI use, make its report available to the Legislature and public, and direct state technology and innovation offices to develop AI policy, training, and service-improvement work.

mandates.title: Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies
mandates.citation: New York State Office of Information Technology Services Policy NYS-P25-001
mandates.summary: New York's acceptable-use policy applies to state entity AI systems that could directly impact the public. It requires leadership approval before adopting new AI systems, identification of an information owner, human oversight for public-impacting decisions, documentation of AI-supported decisions and methods, and periodic assessment for reliability, safety, and fairness.

mandates.title: Executive Order 23-26 and State Government AI Advisory Council Action Plan
mandates.citation: State of Oregon Executive Order 23-26; State Government AI Advisory Council Final Recommended Action Plan
mandates.summary: Oregon established the State Government AI Advisory Council through Executive Order 23-26 and finalized an action plan to guide state-government AI use, recommending executive actions for AI governance, security frameworks, reference architecture, privacy, workforce readiness, and responsible service delivery.

mandates.title: Executive Order 2023-19: Expanding and Governing the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technologies Within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
mandates.summary: Pennsylvania establishes a Generative AI Governing Board and statewide governance values for agency use of generative AI. The order directs responsive and responsible standards intended to prevent generative AI use from enabling activities that violate Commonwealth or federal law.

mandates.title: Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act
mandates.citation: Texas House Bill 149, 89th Legislature, Regular Session
mandates.summary: Texas establishes a regulatory framework for AI systems, including prohibited uses, disclosure and governance requirements, enforcement authority, civil penalties, and a state artificial intelligence council. The enrolled act became effective January 1, 2026.

mandates.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy Act
mandates.summary: Utah creates an Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and Artificial Intelligence Learning Laboratory Program to study AI risks, benefits, impacts, and policy implications, support consumer education, and allow regulatory mitigation agreements for participants using or seeking to use AI technology in the state.
